subject: Clerical Ability
question:
A records officer must file four personnel folders. The names on the folders are:

  A. Gen. Renato Villamor
  B. Atty. Crisanto Banal
  C. Dr. Leonora Quizon
  D. Col. Primo Santos

Which folder is filed FIRST in standard alphabetical order?
explanation: Standard filing rules for personal names require that titles — whether professional (Atty., Dr., Prof.), military (Gen., Col., Lt. Col., Capt.), or honorific (Hon., Rev.) — are placed in parentheses and completely disregarded when determining alphabetical position. Filing is based solely on the surname, then given name. Stripping all titles: Villamor Renato, Banal Crisanto, Quizon Leonora, Santos Primo. Comparing the first letters of each surname: B < Q < S < V. Banal files first, followed by Quizon, Santos, and Villamor. The folder labeled 'Atty. Crisanto Banal' — indexed under BANAL — is filed first = Option B.
steps: Step 1 — Disregard all titles: Gen., Atty., Dr., Col. are not used in indexing.
Step 2 — Index each name by surname: VILLAMOR Renato, BANAL Crisanto, QUIZON Leonora, SANTOS Primo.
Step 3 — Compare surname first letters: B(2) < Q(17) < S(19) < V(22).
Step 4 — Alphabetical order: Banal(1st), Quizon(2nd), Santos(3rd), Villamor(4th).
Step 5 — First folder = Banal = Atty. Crisanto Banal = Option B.

distractorExplanations.A: Gen. Renato Villamor indexes as VILLAMOR — the surname initial 'V' is the latest of the four, placing this folder last, not first. The title 'Gen.' is ignored entirely in filing.
distractorExplanations.C: Dr. Leonora Quizon indexes as QUIZON — 'Q' comes second among the four surnames. This folder is filed second, not first.
distractorExplanations.D: Col. Primo Santos indexes as SANTOS — 'S' ranks third among the four surnames. This folder is filed third, not first.
distractorExplanations.E: Titles such as Engr. are disregarded in filing; by surname, Zamora files last of all — picking it usually means filing by title or by given name.

tip.label: Filing Rule
tip.text: Personal titles — Dr., Atty., Gen., Col., Prof., Rev., Hon. — are IGNORED in alphabetical filing. Strip the title, then sort by surname. 'Dr. Juan Reyes' files under R for Reyes, not D for Doctor.

reference: ARMA International Filing Rules, Rule 6 (Titles and Suffixes in Personal Names).

subject: Clerical Ability
subtopic: Personal Titles Disregarded in Indexing — Mixed Honorifics
question:
A file clerk arranges four folders bearing the following names:

  A. Judge Erlinda Manalastas
  B. Sec. Arturo Dimaculangan
  C. Prof. Nicanor Tagalog
  D. Atty. Melinda Ferrer

Which folder is filed THIRD in correct alphabetical order?
explanation: Under ARMA filing rules, all personal titles — Judge, Secretary (Sec.), Professor (Prof.), Attorney (Atty.), and any similar honorific — are placed in parentheses and disregarded when determining alphabetical position. Only the surname and given name are used for sorting. Indexing each name: Manalastas Erlinda, Dimaculangan Arturo, Tagalog Nicanor, Ferrer Melinda. Comparing surnames: Dimaculangan (D) < Ferrer (F) < Manalastas (M) < Tagalog (T). The filing sequence is Dimaculangan (1st), Ferrer (2nd), Manalastas (3rd), Tagalog (4th). The folder filed third is Manalastas — 'Judge Erlinda Manalastas' = Option A.
steps: Step 1 — Disregard all titles: Judge, Sec., Prof., Atty. are ignored.
Step 2 — Index by surname: MANALASTAS Erlinda, DIMACULANGAN Arturo, TAGALOG Nicanor, FERRER Melinda.
Step 3 — Compare surname first letters: D(4) < F(6) < M(13) < T(20).
Step 4 — Filing order: Dimaculangan(1st), Ferrer(2nd), Manalastas(3rd), Tagalog(4th).
Step 5 — Third folder = Manalastas = Judge Erlinda Manalastas = Option A.

distractorExplanations.B: Sec. Arturo Dimaculangan indexes as DIMACULANGAN — 'D' is the earliest surname initial of the four, placing this folder first, not third.
distractorExplanations.C: Prof. Nicanor Tagalog indexes as TAGALOG — 'T' is the latest surname initial, placing this folder last (fourth), not third.
distractorExplanations.D: Atty. Melinda Ferrer indexes as FERRER — 'F' ranks second among the four surnames. This folder is filed second, not third.
distractorExplanations.E: Disregarding the Dr. title, Urbano (U) files after Tagalog (T) and is last — it tempts examinees who order by title or by given name.

tip.label: Common Mistake
tip.text: Do not let titles pull your eye to the wrong word. In 'Sec. Arturo Dimaculangan', the filing key is DIMACULANGAN — not Sec. and not Arturo. Cover the title and first name with your finger; sort by surname alone.

reference: ARMA International Filing Rules, Rule 6 (Titles and Suffixes in Personal Names).
